title: Punk's Hole (Manorville)
summary: Punk's Hole was a former name for the village known as Manor, now associated with Manorville, or for a nearby hollow. The name combines a local hollow with punk, an Algonquian word used for fungus or tinder from old oak trees and stumps.
history_content: The history preserves a local Manorville name and the woodland explanation attached to it. No dated deed or colonial event is supplied in the available references.
translation_content:
The word punk is explained as a name for fungous growth on old oak trees and stumps, used for fuel or tinder. The full place-name combines that word with the English word hole, meaning a hollow.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names are embedded with meaning about relationships to the land — narrating historical events, conveying traditional knowledges, and revealing connections to identity and culture.”

— Canada's History, Lesson: Indigenous Place Names in Canada (n.d.), PDF page 1, Background
preservation_content: Punk's Hole records how Native-language words remained in local landscape memory, even when combined with English descriptive language and later village naming.
